props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · tint set to teal
props.title: The Shape of a File

B01.visual_intent: Act title 'The Shape of a File' (serif 40) top-left. The real 14-line file `lab-shaders/01-breathe.gdshader` in the code panel at left with line numbers; at right a framed real Godot render that breathes between pale gray and teal. Window label: 'Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · tint set to teal'.
B01.motion_claim: The render swings from pale gray to teal and back while the file stays still beside it.

show.event: file and window on the stage; window labelled
the pulse swings: gray to teal and back

B01.why: The promise of the film is that this file can be read; the real file beside its real result is the claim, and nothing drawn could be as honest.
B01.capture_spec: C01a: Lab rect, lab-shaders/01-breathe.gdshader, --set tint=#5FA391 (the Inspector would set it), live TIME, a clip a little longer than this beat's measured audio (about 16 s) at 30 fps, Forward+, no input. Verified: the pulse swings between about 0.90 gray and (0.38, 0.64, 0.57); period about 3.2 s (evidence/planning-checks/pulse-range.txt). Gate V samples the 50 and 85 percent frames and fails a pale fill on the cream stage, so set --time-origin t0 so that wave = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(2 * (t0 + t)) is 0.4 or less at t = 0.5 and 0.85 times this beat's measured audio (for 16.0 s, t0 about 0.98 s gives 0.11 at both). B40 needs its OWN clip (C01b): one origin cannot serve both beats.

B02.visual_intent: The same 14-line file alone on the stage (layout 'code', line numbers on). Three bands light in turn with a one-word chip beside each: line 1 'header', lines 3 to 4 'globals', lines 6 to 14 'functions'.
B02.motion_claim: A highlight band slides down the file and stops on each zone as the voice names it.
B02.why: A Manim card at the 32-point type floor holds about 8 lines of code (measured: Menlo at 32 is 0.25 unit per character, 0.6 per line); ShaderLab's code layout shows all 14 real lines.

B03.visual_intent: `shader_type canvas_item;` in monospace (size 40) upper center. Under it a row of tiles: `canvas_item` captioned '2D + interface' and `spatial` captioned '3D' (both outlined), and three small tiles `particles`, `sky`, `fog` under a bracket labelled 'more'. A terracotta ring settles on canvas_item, in the line and on its tile. Serif 32 caption: 'shader type: the first line; says what the shader is for'. Last, a dimmer second line `render_mode blend_add;` slides in below with a tag 'optional' and a drawn pair of overlapping outlined squares whose overlap is tinted lighter, labelled 'blend'.
B03.motion_claim: The first line types in and the tiles line up under it; a ring picks canvas item; then an optional second line slides in below.

show.event: render_mode line slides in, tagged optional

B03.why: The first line is the picture; tiles under the real line show what the line chooses, which a table would only list.

B04.visual_intent: A band labelled 'globals' with three rows stacked, each a declaration copied from lab-shaders/04-globals.gdshader in monospace with a serif 32 caption beneath in the GLOSSARY wording: `uniform float level = 0.8;` / 'a value your game sets from outside; every pixel sees the same one'; `const vec3 TEAL = vec3(0.37, 0.64, 0.57);` / 'a named value that never changes'; `varying vec2 corner_uv;` / 'a value set at each corner, blended across the shape for fragment() to read'. Below the band a thin bar labelled 'functions' and a drawn downward arrow from the band into it, labelled 'readable below'. Captions may wrap to two lines.
B04.motion_claim: The three declarations land one by one as they are named; a downward arrow then runs from them into the functions bar.
B04.why: Three declarations with their one-line meanings, and the direction they are visible in, are a structure drawn on cue; a table cannot show the arrow.

props.title: The functions Godot calls
rows: once for each pixel the shape covers
once per pixel, for each light that touches it

B05.visual_intent: A three-row table in the GLOSSARY wording, one row ringed as each function is named: vertex(), fragment(), light().
B05.motion_claim: The ring steps down the rows with the voice; fragment() stays ringed longest.
B05.runner_up: ShaderLab code layout with two labelled ranges
B05.why: Three terms are defined here for the first time, and a table of kinds is exactly what the evidence-table component is for.

props.title: Godot 4.7.2 · shader compile error · printed by the engine

B06.visual_intent: A terminal window titled 'Godot 4.7.2 · shader compile error · printed by the engine' holding the engine's own log of lab-shaders/40-err-semicolon.gdshader, word for word: the source lines around the error with the offending line marked, then the error message. A terracotta ring lands on the marked line (the line AFTER the one missing its semicolon) late in the beat.
B06.motion_claim: The log lines land one by one; a ring then settles on the marked line.

show.event: ring on the marked line: the next line, where Godot noticed

B06.why: The engine's real message beats any retelling; CCPlainShell plays real output verbatim (SHOW-THE-THING). If GATE T flags the dark window, fall back to the cream code card with the same lines.

B07.visual_intent: Top region: one code card that holds one shader in three spellings in turn: neat (the five lines of 02-spacing-neat), squeezed (two lines: `shader_type canvas_item;` then `void fragment(){COLOR=vec4(0.4+0.6*UV,0.7,1.0);}`, 48 characters, the widest line), and spread (the seven lines of 02-spacing-spread). The characters slide and the line breaks collapse and reopen as one spelling becomes the next. Bottom region, never changing: ONE framed real Godot render (lab_window of png/02-spacing-neat.png, a pastel gradient) captioned 'Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+', with a drawn equals sign (two short bars) between code and picture, labelled 'same picture'. Type at least 32; keep the card inside 12 units.
B07.motion_claim: The code is rewritten three times while the picture below it never changes.

show.event: neat collapses into the squeezed spelling
squeezed opens into the spread spelling

B07.runner_up: ShaderLab stack layout with one spelling
B07.why: Three spellings and one unchanging picture can only be told by a transformation; a static code panel shows one spelling.

B08.visual_intent: Left: the nine-line card of lab-shaders/03-comment-on.gdshader with a block comment above the function and a trailing `// soften` comment: both comment spans are grayed from the first frame. Right: a framed real render (lab_window of png/03-comment-on.png, the pastel gradient). Then `//` is typed at the start of the line `c = 0.4 + 0.6 * c;` (the line grays out, as in lab-shaders/03-comment-off.gdshader) and the render cross-fades to the real png/03-comment-off.png (the same colors, much more saturated, dark top-left corner). Captions: 'line comment', 'block comment'.
B08.motion_claim: Typing two slashes grays a line out and the picture beside the code changes at once.

show.event: code with both comment kinds grayed; pastel render
`//` typed at the start of the c line
render cross-fades to the saturated picture

B08.why: A commented-out line changing the picture is the claim, and it needs code and a real result changing together.

B09.visual_intent: Two panels. Left: two name tags in monospace, `level` with a drawn check and `Level` with a drawn cross, a drawn capital-L highlight on the difference. Right: `gl_FragColor` with a drawn cross, a drawn arrow to `COLOR` with a drawn check, captioned 'Godot's name for the output'. Top caption in serif 32: 'GLSL: the OpenGL Shading Language; Godot's is close to GLSL ES 3.0'. No engine messages on screen (the narration says unknown identifier).
B09.motion_claim: A cross lands on the wrong-case name and on the other language's name; the check lands on Godot's.

show.event: cross on Level, capital L highlighted
gl_FragColor crossed; arrow to COLOR; check

B09.why: Two kinds of wrong name (wrong case, other language) are a contrast of name tags with marks; the logs for both were run and are in the evidence.
